newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Brazil's Melles sees steady rise in coffee output.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Melles sees steady rise in coffee output.

text.p: Brazil's annual coffee output should total about 25 to 30 million 60-kg bags over the next five years, Carlos Melles, a Brazilian lawmaker and expert on his country's coffee trade, said Thursday.
Melles, a congressman respresenting the coffee-rich state of Minas Gerais, said output should eventually climb back up to the yearly average of 35 million bags that Brazil produced in the 1980s.
But he added that a current lack of financing for the coffee sector, coupled with high production costs and interest rates, was putting a damper on potential output.

Melles, a former head of Brazil's leading coffee growers' federation, estimated that output in the 1996/97 coffee year, which ends next October, could be as much as 20 percent less than the 25 million bags that he said Brazil produced in the 1995/1996 coffee year.
He gave no specific figures, but said the country is currently sitting on about 12 million bags in stocks.
